dependency_text: The order count, orientability and census of CELL-SIGN; the strict choices of ENCODED-READERS; the growth and birth choices of LOCAL-COMMUTE.
objective: At the owner's go-ahead ("Yes continue") on direction 1 of CELL-SIGN-20261127-001: at all 1,819 grown closures (open census starts, four rounds), list every minimal strict even choice and test whether each is orientable; list the census types' non-orientable even choices and measure what they need (knots holding values, their shapes); test whether size explains why growth's closures make the sign exactly non-orientability. G18 Comparing growth laws. Stop when every frozen prediction is scored.
status: Complete 2026-11-28 (capability gained; exhaustive listings, built starts and sampled starts; referee pending): a non-orientable even choice covered twice needs six failing pairs, three kinds at six, each putting two values on one pair of knots below seven pairs (P1); the census starts' bounds keep them out of growth's closures through the birth rule (doubled meetings only between start knots) and the join rule (census start 6830 stalls); with one more start knot or distinction growth makes them (P2), and sampled starts of six to eight knots do at 3 of 1,283 closures (P3).
stop_rule: Stop when every frozen prediction is scored; no growth law is changed.
title: Why are growth's even strict choices orientable?
